purpose: Evidence-backed links from frozen novena identities to Customs Atlas customs and shared geography context. No proximity-based association.
invariants: A novena does not become local merely because a shrine or custom is associated with its devotional family.
Exact-form attestation and devotional-family context are distinct relationship types.
PLACE_PENDING and AREA_CONTEXT never become canonical map pins without promotion through the shared Geography SOT.
Directory/TLM community proximity never proves a novena custom.

links.note: The Sacred Heart novena belongs to the same devotional family as family consecration; the exact frozen AO prayer form is not claimed to be the Paray form. Promoted to the canonical shared Paray place/shrine after SHRINES_PILGRIMAGES_SOT_V1.

Paray explicitly recommends a Sacred Heart novena as possible preparation for home enthronement; enthronement remains a distinct custom. Promoted to the canonical shared Paray place/shrine after SHRINES_PILGRIMAGES_SOT_V1.
Prayerful cemetery visitation is related to prayer for the faithful departed but is not required by the novena.
2 November prayer for the dead is a privileged contextual observance; the novena itself may be prayed at other times.
Official Lisieux material attests a St Thérèse novena and the shrine context. It does not prove that the sanctuary uses AO's exact Twenty-Four Glory Bes form.
French episcopal evidence attests multiple St Joseph sanctuaries and feast devotion; it does not establish the exact Moran novena at each place.

negative_knowledge.reason: No row-level evidence-backed Customs/Geography bridge has yet been established for the exact novena or a sufficiently relevant devotional-family context. Do not infer one from nearby shrines or TLM venues.
